maya: Heads up — the leaderboard chart in the console is showing experiment lines swapping colors and labels for the new int8 bring-up. Screenshot in thread. Looks like display/legend mismatch vs csv export :confused:

raj: I noticed this too. In the UI the legend shows A/B correctly, but when I export CSV the rows are in a different order so the exported diff tool assigns the wrong baseline.

chen: Repro locally. If you compare the series order in the series array vs the exported CSV header it doesn't match when run_id contains special chars (we have run-2025-03 and run_2025). Dump below:

```csv
run_id,seed,rouge_l,accuracy
run_2025,42,0.512,0.85
run-2025-03,42,0.498,0.83
run+q4,42,0.490,0.82
```

raj: Huh. Could be a change in python dict ordering in the exporter or we started relying on insertion order that isn't stable across processes. CI upgraded the exporter package last week. :thinking:

ci-bot: exporter job 1934567888 completed: exporter v0.9.3 -> v0.9.4 deployed to staging. No runtime errors, but CSV sample size decreased by 1% (info).

maya: I dug a bit on the frontend side: we sort visible series by `displayName` for the legend, but the CSV exporter (backend) sorts columns by raw `run_id` string. When run_id includes quant tags like `+q4` the lexical order differs from the display name order. So UI vs CSV can diverge.

chen: Proposed minimal fix (frontend + exporter canonical sort): ensure both use same canonical comparator. Quick patch I used in prototype (frontend):

```js
// ensure series order consistent with exporter
const canonicalKey = (s) => s.labels?.display_name || s.run_id || ''
series.sort((a,b) => canonicalKey(a).localeCompare(canonicalKey(b)))
```

raj: That looks good. We should also add tests on the exporter side: unit test verifying CSV header order equals UI ordering for a few weird run_id cases (`run-2025-03`, `run_2025`, `run+q4`). Also add an e2e snapshot for the scorecard CSV export.

maya: I'll open a small PR with the frontend change + test vector and assign @ben for review. Also tagging @eng-ml for visibility.

ben: ack, will review tomorrow. One more ask: can we add an integration check in CI to fail if header ordering changes between runs? A lightweight assert would catch regressions.

sre-bot: Canary deploy for exporter scheduled at 2025-03-12 12:30 UTC. Will monitor error rates and CSV size diffs.

maya: Thanks — sounds good. I'll include the CI assertion in the PR and link the failing case so we can triage if the canary flags anything. :thumbsup:
